text.p: PAX World Management Co, the adviser to the PAX World Fund, said it was sold to members of the Shadek family of New Jersey.
PAX World is a "socially responsible," no-load mutual fund, with more than $500 million in assets.
PAX said Luther Tyson, one of the four selling co-founders, will continue as fund president. Anthony Brown, another founder, will continue as portfolio manager.

"The Shadek family was a good fit," Tyson said in a statement. "Other offers were more renumerative, but we decided to accept the Shadek offer on the deep belief that the standards we set for the last 26 years will be met and exceeded by the new owners."
Lawrence Shadek, 46, an executive vice president of H.G. Wellington & Co Inc, is the new chairman.
"Shareholders will see a younger management seeking to improve performance and, at the same time, sustaining the present socially responsible criteria," Shadek said.
PAX World's investment objective is to buy a diversified portfolio of stocks that offer primarily income and conservation of principal and long-term growth of capital.
